transcript: Last night, my sister and I saw An Enemy of The People on Broadway. This is a pretty old play, but do not be fooled, it feels very relevant and this new version by Amy Herzog is concise and pointed. Jeremy Strong plays a doctor who makes a troubling discovery about his town's water. This is the springboard from which the play’s big themes emerge: corruption, censorship, political agendas, free thought or the lack thereof. Even though this production has big name actors like Jeremy Strong, Michael Imperioli, and Victoria Pedretti, their performances aren't particularly flashy. They all give great performances that really let the play speak for itself. The play is very allegorical, and feels somewhat ancient Greek theatery, with how it speaks to the audience so urgently. And even the choice to produce this in the Circle in The Square makes you feel not very distant from these characters and the issues that they're confronting, because they're yours too. This play makes you consider from where you seek truth, or rather, who you choose to believe. Overall I thought it was great — it feels urgent, relevant, compelling — all things that a lot of great theater pieces do. With that, another playbill for my collection.
